newsitem.title: GERMANY: SMH bank changes focus, reduces credit business.
newsitem.headline: SMH bank changes focus, reduces credit business.

text.p: Schroeder Muenchmeyer Hengst & Co, one of the Frankfurt's best-known private banks, on Tuesday said it was pulling out of the credit activities which pushed the institution to the edge of financial collapse in the 1980s.
SMH, now controlled by Britain's Lloyds Bank group, said in a statement it planned to cut its workforce by 10 percent and would focus primarily on investment banking in future.

Its lending business would be scaled down and the focus shifted to three core activities -- institutional brokerage, asset management and retail securities business. It also planned to expand corporate finance and dealing business.

The bank said it would no longer grant loans carrying "entrepreneurial risk", but approve only those backed with water-tight guarantees and that its lending business would in future merely support other activities.
The restructuring would play to its strengths, the bank said: "SMH is convinced that this will lay the basis for a successful future."

The decision to pull out of higher risk lending marks the logical end to a sequence of events triggered when the bank ran close to financial collapse in the 1980's when one of its major creditors, engineering group IBH, collapsed.
Lloyds, which stepped in to help the German bank get back on its feet, now owns 75 percent of SMH.

The bank has gradually rebuilt its profitability and has continually managed to pay a dividend to its owners over the last few years. In 1995, it distributed 6.5 million marks ($4.23 million) of profits after reporting a profit of 26.1 million marks.
It employed 450 people at the end of 1995.
SMH said its new strategic focus would leave it concentrating on its most profitable areas.
One of SMH's co-owners, Eberhard Weyershaeuser, would leave the bank at the end of 1996 as his areas of operation were being discontinued with the end of the credit activities.
His role as joint speaker for the management board would be taken over by Ulrich Schuette, SMH said.
But it added that Weyershaeuser, who joined SMH from Westdeutsche Landesbank some years ago, would continue to support the bank and had been instrumental in developing its new direction.
Jochen Neynaber, Ulrich Schuette und Adolf Kraus would remain members of the management board, SMH said. They would be joined by Andreas Huebner and Andreas Muth.
